cards.title: One correct form
cards.body: Each stem is written so only one aspect fits. Read the whole line — count, finished result, or unfinished process.
cards.body_cz: Každá věta je napsaná tak, aby seděl jen jeden aspekt. Čti celý řádek — počet, hotový výsledek, nebo nedokončený proces.
points: I have written three emails — here they are. (result / count)
I have been writing emails all morning and I still have two left. (process)

cards.title: Form table
cards.body: Same perfect idea (link to now) — two shapes:
cards.body_cz: Stejná idea perfectu (vazba na teď) — dva tvary:

table.caption: Present perfect simple vs continuous
rows: how many / already / done / result now
how long / for / since / all… / still going

points: Simple: have written · has finished · haven't done
Continuous: have been writing · has been waiting · haven't been sleeping

cards.title: Simple = result / count / done
cards.body: have/has + past participle. Focus on finished outcome or how many.
cards.body_cz: have/has + příčestí. Důraz na hotový výsledek nebo kolikrát / kolik.
points: She has read the whole report — she can answer now.
How many emails have you sent today?

cards.title: Continuous = process / duration
cards.body: have/has been + -ing. Activity over time; often still going or visible now.
cards.body_cz: have/has been + -ing. Činnost v čase; často pořád běží nebo je teď vidět.
points: She has been reading for an hour and she is only on page two.
How long have you been waiting?

cards.title: How many vs How long
cards.body: Question words often choose the aspect for you:
cards.body_cz: Tázací slova často zvolí aspekt za tebe:

rows: How many times have you visited Prague?
How long have you been waiting here?

points: Some items only blank Have (not Did) in the question — that is aux choice, not the full form contrast
Most items blank the full form: have written vs have been writing

cards.title: Check options
cards.body: On full-form items you always see four structures: past simple · present perfect simple · present perfect continuous · one wrong form. Exactly one fits the stem.
cards.body_cz: U plných tvarů vždy čtyři struktury: past simple · PP simple · PP continuous · jeden špatný tvar. Sedí právě jeden.

cards.title: Type
cards.body: (verb) = base form. Type the full correct structure for the blank — not only -ing, not a different verb.
cards.body_cz: (verb) = základ. Do mezery piš celou správnou strukturu — ne jen -ing, ne jiné sloveso.
points: I ____ (write) emails all morning… → have been writing

cards.title: Both can look possible — trust the stem
cards.title_cz: Obojí může vypadat možné — věř větě
cards.body: Without a forcing detail, English sometimes allows both aspects. In this unit the extra words (still only halfway, right now, once and left, every hour…) pick one. Do not invent the other form.
cards.body_cz: Bez nápovědy angličtina někdy dovolí oba aspekty. Tady extra slova (pořád jen v půlce, právě teď, jednou a odešly…) volí jeden. Nevymýšlej druhý tvar.

cards.title: Czech trap
cards.body: Czech often one present for both ideas. English chooses done result vs ongoing process.
cards.body_cz: Čeština často jeden přítomný čas pro obojí. Angličtina volí hotový výsledek vs probíhající proces.
